extraction.document_summary: GREAT Critical Cover Series by Great Eastern is presented as a health insurance product focused on critical illness coverage that can continue beyond a first payout, including protection “over and over again” for recurring critical illnesses. The brochure emphasizes that some critical illnesses can recur and may raise the risk of developing a second or third critical illness, and the product is positioned to help manage financial impact from repeated episodes. The document includes several important “Important Notes” clarifications, including that all ages are “age next birthday,” and that it has “no savings or investment feature,” so “there is no cash value if the policy ends or is terminated prematurely.” It also notes figures are illustrative and “not a contract of insurance,” with terms specified in the policy contract.
quality_notes: The provided Markdown contains only high-level marketing statements and Important Notes; it does not state the critical illness benefit structure, claim mechanics (e.g., number of claims supported, recurrence/waiting/survival rules), policy term, coverage limits, or eligibility/underwriting requirements.
No plan tiers/options, benefit amounts, deductibles, co-insurance, age ranges, or renewal rules are specified in the text provided.

policies.quick_summary: Critical illness coverage intended to pay repeatedly for recurring critical illnesses beyond the first claim. No savings/investment feature, and the document provides only general marketing descriptions plus Important Notes without technical coverage details or limits in the provided text extract. Ages refer to age next birthday; figures are illustrative and terms are in the policy contract; protected up to specified limits by SDIC (per brochure). There is no stated entry/max age, term length, claim limits, or payout amounts in the provided content excerpt, so specific benefit mechanics cannot be reliably extracted.
coverage_scope: Critical illness coverage that continues over and over again beyond a first claim (as described in marketing text)
important_caveats: This is described as an advertisement/general information; it is not a contract of insurance and the precise terms are in the policy contract.
